title: Can a traffic fine expire under the statute of limitations?
excerpt: Traffic fines do not last forever. We explain what the statute of limitations is, why dates and notices matter, and when to have your case reviewed.
body:
Having old traffic tickets or fines can prevent you, for example, from registering the transfer of a vehicle. But traffic penalties cannot be collected indefinitely.

## What is the statute of limitations?

It is the loss of the authority's right to collect a penalty when it lets the legally established time pass without acting. The National Traffic Code (Law 769 of 2002, article 159) governs this period for traffic penalties.

## Why dates matter

The period can be interrupted by certain actions of the authority, such as a payment order within a coercive collection process. That is why knowing whether a fine has expired is not just about its age: you need to review **the dates of the ticket, the penalty and each notice**.

## Other options

Besides the statute of limitations, there are other grounds to request the removal of a ticket, such as expiration or errors in identifying the offender, for example in cases of identity theft or cloned license plates.

## How do you know if your case qualifies?

Check your account status on SIMIT and review the information with a lawyer before paying or signing payment agreements.
